name: How does a tub-to-shower conversion compare to keeping a traditional bathtub for accessibility?

mainEntity.name: How does a tub-to-shower conversion compare to keeping a traditional bathtub for accessibility?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard tub often creates a major tripping hazard because of its high threshold, whereas a walk-in shower eliminates or minimizes that barrier. Walk-in or curbless showers allow easy entry on foot or with mobility aids. When replacing a tub, you gain seamless entry, custom slip-resistant tile flooring, and space for integrated shower benches and recessed niches. The trade-off is the loss of a soaking tub, so homeowners planning a bathroom remodel often choose to retain one bathtub elsewhere in the home while converting the primary bath into a zero-barrier shower for accessible daily use.
acceptedAnswer.description: A tub-to-shower conversion removes high step-over barriers, providing safer zero-threshold access, custom tile benches, and slip-resistant floors compared to traditional tubs.
